notable_features.text: Polish marks grammatical distinctions through a complex case system typical of Slavic languages, and it has a rich consonant inventory of 37 phonemes, including many palatalized and affricate sounds. It strictly follows SVO word order and encodes two WALS tense/aspect categories, reflecting the Slavic emphasis on verbal aspect. Socially, Polish requires strict T–V distinction and obligatory honorifics, making formality a grammatically enforced part of addressing others.
